question_text: Balance Sheet of M/s P and Q as on 31st March 2012 given. Mr. R to be admitted for 1/4 share from 1st April 2012. Goodwill to be valued at 3 years purchase of average profits from last 5 years.
requirements: 1) Prepare P&L Account for year ended 31st March 2013, 2) Prepare Balance Sheet of Company as on 1st April 2013
key_points: Working notes showing goodwill calculation, Partners Capital Accounts, Share distribution, Cash balance, Depreciation calculations

question_text: X Ltd. and Y Ltd. amalgamate to form XY Ltd. Detailed balance sheets of both companies given. Shares to be issued at premium. Assets and liabilities taken at book values.
requirements: Prepare realization accounts in the books of X Ltd and Y Ltd to close their books.
key_points: Working notes for purchase consideration, Valuation adjustments for debtors and stock, Calculation of shares to be issued

question_text: Rajan (Pvt) Ltd has Head Office and Branch in Chitwan. Goods sent from HO to Branch at cost plus 10%. HO makes gross profit of 33.33% on selling price.
requirements: Prepare memorandum Trading and P&L Account of Head Office and Branch in columnar form for year ended 31st Ashad 2079.
key_points: Calculation of opening/closing stock, Unrealized profit elimination, Cost price calculation, Gross profit determination

question_text: Trial Balance of proprietorship firm XYA given with multiple adjusting items including opening stock revaluation, pilferage, furniture destruction.
requirements: 1) Prepare Trading and P&L Account for year ended 31st December 2016, 2) Prepare Balance Sheet as at that date
key_points: Opening stock adjustment, Depreciation calculation, Provision for doubtful debts, Bad debts, Suspense account adjustment

question_text: X purchased 3 plants from Y on hire purchase basis. Cash price Rs 100,000 each. Depreciation 20% diminishing balance (hire purchaser), 30% (hire vendor).
requirements: 1) Agreed value of 2 plants taken back, 2) Book value of plant left, 3) Profit/loss to hire purchaser, 4) Profit/loss on resale
key_points: Depreciation calculation year by year, Agreed value at 30% diminishing balance, Book value at 20% depreciation, Profit/loss determination

question_text: Financial ratios given: Current Ratio 2, Working Capital Rs 400,000, Capital Block to Current Asset 3:2, Fixed Assets to Turnover 1:3.
requirements: Prepare the Financial Position (Capital & Liabilities statement and Assets statement) based on the ratios given.
key_points: Solving simultaneous equations from ratios, Calculation of share capital, turnover, net profit, reserve, cash, debtors, stock, creditors

question_text: Liquidator has Rs 330,000. Capital: 30,000 10% Preference Shares Rs 10 each, 3 classes of 30,000 Equity Shares each with different face and paid-up values.
requirements: Prepare Liquidators Final Statement of Accounts showing receipt and payment.
key_points: Calculation of calls made, Deficiency percentage, Refund and call amounts for each share class

question_text: Company dispatched goods worth Rs 10 crore through bank for collection. Documents not cleared after 15 days normal collection period.
requirements: Should revenue be recognized? Explain with reference to NAS-18.
key_points: Recognition criteria per NAS-18: Transfer of risks and rewards, Effective control, Probable economic benefits, Reliable measurement

question_text: 600 units raw material A at Rs 120 (cost), replacement Rs 90. 500 units partly finished at Rs 260 per unit, additional cost Rs 60. 1500 units finished product X at Rs 320 per unit, selling price Rs 300.
requirements: Determine how each inventory item will be valued as on 31-3-2079. Calculate total inventory value.
key_points: Application of lower of cost and NRV rule, Calculation of NRV for partly finished goods, Write-down to replacement cost

question_text: AD Limited exported goods for $10,000 on 20.2.2078, settled on 20.5.2078. Exchange rates: 20.2 Rs 110, 31.3 Rs 115, 20.5 Rs 112.
requirements: Give journal entries on transaction date, year end and settlement date.
key_points: Exchange gain/loss calculation, Treatment of monetary items, Debtor revaluation at closing rate

question_text: Write short notes on: a) Off Balance Sheet Items, b) Capital Fund in Banks, c) Held for Trading Investments, d) Recognition of Premium Income by Insurance Companies, e) Inter-departmental transfers
requirements: 5 short notes of 3 marks each.
key_points: Off-balance sheet: Contingent assets/liabilities. Capital Fund: Tier-I and Tier-II. HTI: Short-term fluctuation gains. Premium: Cash basis recognition. Inter-departmental: Transfer pricing

question_text: Subhakamana Sugar Mills closed for 11 months. Will take 2 years to restart. Substantial modification cost needed. Bank issued auction notice if loan not repaid in 3 months.
requirements: As an auditor, give your opinion with explanation on the going concern issue.
key_points: NSA 570 requirements, Assessment of going concern, Material uncertainties, Modified opinion possibility, Management assessment evaluation

question_text: Palpa Limited: Inventory Rs 8,500 destroyed, Rs 7,000 given to NGO free, Rs 5,400 damaged and can be reworked at Rs 900 and sold for Rs 4,300.
requirements: As auditor, give opinion on the inventory items not considered in accounts.
key_points: NAS-2 requirements for inventory write-off, Expense recognition timing, Calculation of loss amounts, Proper accounting treatment

question_text: Dharan Limited acquired machine for Rs 80,000 in 2071. Useful life 8 years, straight line depreciation. In 2078/79, technical examination shows remaining life 5 years.
requirements: As auditor, give opinion on the depreciation treatment by the accountant.
key_points: NAS-8 change in estimate, Prospective accounting, Revised depreciation calculation, Carrying amount determination

question_text: Himalaya Fashion has 115 shareholders including 11 employees in FY 2075/76.
requirements: As auditor for FY 2075/76, comment on the shareholder situation.
key_points: Companies Act section 9(1) amendment 2074: Max 101 shareholders (excluding employees), Non-compliance consequence, Auditor responsibility

question_text: After statutory audit completion, fraud detected at auditee office. Management claims auditor failed to detect fraud.
requirements: Give comments on the management's allegation with reference to NSA 240.
key_points: NSA 240: Primary responsibility of management, Reasonable assurance vs absolute, Inherent audit limitations, Sophistication of fraud, Auditor liability conditions

question_text: Auditor cannot obtain evidence on Rs 1 lakh business promotion expense. Company earned Rs 1 billion profit with Rs 10 billion assets. Management claims expense is genuine but invoices misplaced.
requirements: Comment on auditor's decision to qualify the audit report. Is it appropriate?
key_points: NSA 705 modification criteria, Materiality assessment (1 lakh vs 1 billion profit), Immaterial misstatement implications, Management letter alternative

question_text: CA K (reappointed auditor) wants management to reconfirm written representations about their financial statement preparation responsibilities.
requirements: Under what circumstances can auditor ask management to reconfirm responsibilities in written representations?
key_points: NSA 580 circumstances: Changed responsible persons, Prepared in previous year, Indication of misunderstanding, Changed circumstances

question_text: Auditor requested client to pay 70% of previous year audit fee before signing current year audit report. Client lodged disciplinary complaint.
requirements: Comment on the auditor's request with reference to Code of Ethics.
key_points: Code of Ethics section 410.7: Overdue fees create self-interest threat, Permissible safeguards, Partial payment allowed, Independence maintenance requirement

question_text: Explain circumstances when external auditor can use the work of internal audit function.
requirements: Explain the evaluation criteria and when internal audit work can be used.
key_points: NSA 610: Organizational status evaluation, Competence level assessment, Systematic approach evaluation, Objectivity assessment, Risk of audit quality

question_text: Define error and briefly discuss the types of errors.
requirements: What are the different types of errors in financial statements?
key_points: Self-revealing vs not self-revealing, Unintentional vs intentional (fraud), Unconcealed vs concealed errors, Examples of each type

question_text: Define external confirmation as audit evidence and its types.
requirements: What are the types of external confirmations?
key_points: Definition of external confirmation, Positive confirmation (response required), Negative confirmation (response if disagree), Evidence reliability

question_text: Chartered Accountant firm approached by Lalita Sports Club to sponsor a sports event. Is sponsorship allowed?
requirements: Is the firm allowed to sponsor the event as per ICAN Code of Ethics?
key_points: Guidelines on marketing professional services, Sponsorship of charitable organizations, Display of simple banner, Permission when done properly

question_text: PRR & Associates published website with client portfolio, testimonials, and service details.
requirements: Comment on the website content with reference to Code of Ethics.
key_points: Code of Ethics prohibition on solicitation, Client portfolio display restrictions, Testimonial prohibition, Disciplinary action risk

question_text: Kriti Associates appointed for Risk Management Service. Bank agreed to pay Rs 32 Lakh if operational risk fixed below 5 out of 10.
requirements: Comment on this fee arrangement with reference to ICAN Code of Ethics.
key_points: Definition of contingent fees, Prohibition in audit engagements, Threats in non-audit services, Materiality test, Outcome dependency

question_text: Kohalpur Limited (GON substantial investment) completed AGM but failed to appoint auditor due to lack of consultation from Auditor General.
requirements: How can the company appoint the auditor?
key_points: Audit Act 2075 section 11, Companies Act 2063 section 113, Auditor General consultation requirement, CRO appointment authority

question_text: CBB & Associates issued audit report on 15th Bhadra 2079. Later revealed auditor did not renew COP on 30th Asoj 2079.
requirements: Comment on the validity of the audit report.
key_points: Nepal CA Act section 29: No audit service without valid COP, Audit report validity implications, Disciplinary action consequences

question_text: Tolerable misstatement
requirements: Write short notes on: a) Examination in Depth, b) Peer Review, c) Government Audit, d) Tolerable Misstatement
key_points: 4 short notes of 2.5 marks each.
column15: Examination in depth: Follow transaction through flow. Peer Review: Quality assurance system. Government Audit: Financial and performance audit. Tolerable: Margin for undetected misstatement

question_text: Distinguish between Batch Processing and Online Real Time (OLRT) Processing System in computerized environment.
requirements: What are the differences between batch and OLRT processing?
key_points: Batch: Accumulated and processed in groups. OLRT: Processed as they occur. File structure, Update timing, Reporting capability, Audit trail differences

question_text: Distinguish between Accounting Policies and Accounting Estimates.
requirements: What is the difference between policy changes and estimate changes?
key_points: Nature: Principles vs judgments. Changes: Retrospective vs prospective. Examples: FIFO to weighted average vs depreciation method change

question_text: Mr. Madan, director of Manakamana Limited, appoints proxy Mr. Lila Raj to attend AGM in capacity of director.
requirements: Is the appointment of proxy valid? Explain with reference to Companies Act 2063.
key_points: Companies Act section 68: Director must be present. Section 71: Proxy for shareholders. Proxy as director invalid. Not shareholder capacity issue

question_text: Rita Pradhan signed prospectus with reservations. Prospectus contains false contents causing investor loss.
requirements: What relief can Rita Pradhan claim? Explain with reference to Companies Act 2063.
key_points: Companies Act section 24: Director liability for false statements. Relief if: Resign before publication, Publish notice of false statement, Prove ignorance. Notice publication requirement

question_text: Board wants to remove auditor on ground of disclaimer opinion on fixed assets due to non-provision of details.
requirements: Examine validity of removal proceedings with reference to Companies Act 2063.
key_points: Companies Act section 119: Removal grounds - breach of conduct, act against company interest, act contrary to law. Disclaimer opinion not valid ground. Auditor cannot be removed

question_text: National Insurance Company wants to issue Further Public Offering (FPO) at premium.
requirements: Advise on pre-conditions and procedures for issuing FPO at premium citing Companies Act 2063.
key_points: Companies Act section 29: Conditions - Made profits 3 consecutive years, Net worth > liabilities, General meeting approval. Subsection 3: Use of premium account

question_text: Namaste Telecom wants to convert from public to private limited company.
requirements: Assist with conversion process under Companies Act 2063.
key_points: Companies Act section 14: Circumstances - Shareholders < 7 or paid-up capital not maintained. Process: Amend memorandum and articles, Apply to CRO within 30 days, Conversion certificate within 60 days

question_text: Taranath Rai, NRB director, facing removal application due to past CEO expulsion for security over-valuation causing bank loss.
requirements: What are conditions for NRB director removal? Can removal proceed on this ground?
key_points: NRB Act 2058 section 22(5): Removal grounds - Disqualification, Lack of capability, Act causing loss to banking system, Dishonesty, License revocation, Absence from meetings. Past act not ground for removal

question_text: Mr. Shisir Chand appointed as auditor of Manaslu Bank Ltd for the first time. What matters should be included in auditor's report?
requirements: State matters to be included in bank auditor's report per Bank and Financial Institution Act 2073.
key_points: Act section 66(3): Queries response, Financial statement format compliance, Accuracy of records, Misconduct/irregularity/loss, Credit write-off compliance, Transaction satisfaction, Shareholder matters, Other prescribed matters

question_text: Mr. Dhakal, Nepal Commercial Bank CEO, seeks information about NRB loan and refinancing provisions.
requirements: Make recommendations about NRB lending and refinancing per NRB Act 2058.
key_points: NRB Act section 49(1): Loan/refinance to commercial banks max 1 year against securities - international negotiable instruments, Government bonds, Deposits/gold, Bills/promissory notes. Section 49(2): Other credit 1 year if public interest and Government guarantee. Section 49(3): Renewal possible

question_text: No person can operate insurance business without certificate. State conditions when registration of insurer may be cancelled.
requirements: Under what circumstances can insurance registration be cancelled per Insurance Act 2049?
key_points: Insurance Act 2049 section 13: Cancellation grounds - Business not started within 6 months, Liability > assets, Court decision not fulfilled in 3 months, Unequal facilities vs foreign insurer, No office in Nepal, Functions not performed per Act. Board provides reasonable time for clarification

question_text: Group of young graduates wanting to start securities business in Nepal approach for advice on licensing requirements.
requirements: State license requirements and matters to specify when applying for securities business license per Securities Act 2063.
key_points: Securities Act section 56: License mandatory for securities business. Section 57: Required matters - Type of securities business, Agent appointment, Stock exchange recommendation, Ability to carry business. Apply to Securities Board

question_text: Employees of Barahi Motors Ltd demanded advance bonus which was refused. Board unable to decide without balance sheet.
requirements: Advise on conditions and procedures for advance bonus distribution per Bonus Act 2030.
key_points: Bonus Act 2030 section 11: If balance sheet not submitted, distribute tentative 5% minimum of net income. Later adjust after final assessment. Excess deduct in next year assessment

question_text: State allowed deductions from worker remuneration per Labor Act 2074.
requirements: What deductions are allowed from worker remuneration per Labor Act 2074?
key_points: Labor Act 2074 section 38: Allowed deductions - Tax/fees, Provident fund/insurance/social security contribution, Court/judicial order, Prescribed services/facilities, Absence period, Loss/damage of employer property, Collective agreement amounts, Union fees, Loan/advance provided

question_text: State circumstances when a councilor ceases office and how vacant post is filled per Nepal CA Act 2053.
requirements: When does a councilor's post become vacant and how is vacancy filled?
key_points: Nepal CA Act 2053 section 8(1): Cessation - Ceases membership, Resignation accepted, 3 consecutive meeting absence, Term expires, Non-compliance with conduct, Death. Vacancy: <1 year remaining - designation; >1 year - election

question_text: Define Certificate of Practice (COP). Why is it required per Nepal CA Act 2053?
requirements: What is COP and why is it required?
key_points: Nepal CA Act 2053 section 2(j): COP is certificate to render accounting profession. Section 28: Member applies to Institute with fees, Council provides COP after fulfilling conditions. Required: No member can carry audit profession without valid COP

question_text: State legal provisions regarding fund, account and auditing of Social Welfare Council.
requirements: What are the legal provisions for Social Welfare Council fund and auditing?
key_points: Social Welfare Act 2049 section 17: Fund contains GON money, Foreign assistance through GON, Property income, Donations/assistance, Other sources. Section 18: Accounts per Government procedures, Audit by Auditor General, Government inspection right, Council inspection of affiliated organizations

question_text: Mention provisions related to mitigation of adverse environmental effects per Industrial Enterprises Act 2076.
requirements: What are the provisions for environmental effect mitigation?
key_points: Industrial Enterprises Act 2076 section 7: EIA/IEE required before operation if required by law, Carried out when increasing capital/capacity/changing objective, Industry responsible for mitigation, Monitoring by industry registration body, Self-declaration if not required

question_text: Under what circumstances cannot insurance registration certificate be renewed per Insurance Act 2049?
requirements: When cannot insurance certificate be renewed?
key_points: Insurance Act 2049 section 11A: Cannot renew if - Balance sheet not submitted, Income statement not submitted, Auditor report not submitted, Actuary report not submitted, Insurance service fee not paid, Prohibited from business. Board notifies within 15 days

question_text: Highlight legal provisions relating to lay-off period and remuneration per Labor Act 2074.
requirements: What are lay-off provisions and remuneration?
key_points: Labor Act 2074 section 15: Lay-off max 15 days, employer can stop work due to shortage/inability. Section 39: Workers laid off receive half remuneration until work resumes. Employment continues during lay-off

topic_2: What are the main functions of WTO?
topic_3: WTO functions: Implement covered agreements, Provide negotiation forum, Administer dispute settlement, Administer trade policy review, Cooperate with IMF/IBRD for policy coherence, Assist developing countries

question_text: Write short note on Establishment of Nepal Securities Board.
requirements: Explain the establishment and structure of Nepal Securities Board.
key_points: Securities Act 2063 section 3: Established to regulate securities market and protect investor interests. Consists of: Chairperson (GON), Joint Secretaries (Finance, Law), NRB representative, ICAN representative, FNCCI representative, Expert nominee (3 years tenure)

question_text: Write short note on Promissory Note as per Negotiable Instruments Act 2034.
requirements: Define and explain promissory note.
key_points: Negotiable Instruments Act 2034 section 2(f): Written instrument (not government/bank note) containing unconditional promise signed by maker to pay certain sum to certain person or bearer. Must include: writing, express promise, unconditional, money only, maker signature, certainty of parties
